title: Pencil Icon with Heading

illustrates.quote: Icons may be used with headings or within text to indicate specific types of text, e.g., important facts, essay questions, etc. (See UEB, §3.22, Shapes and §11.7.2, Transcriber-Defined Shapes.) The icon (shape indicator and letters) is preceded and followed by a blank space. Icons follow print for placement, e.g., preceding or following a heading.

blocks.features: Bold italic serif heading, flanked by em-dashes, preceded by a small pencil-icon graphic.

print.notes: Illustrates a print icon (a pencil graphic) placed before a heading, transcribed in braille as a transcriber-defined shape indicator plus letters, preceded and followed by a blank space, per rule 4.9.1.
print.printFeatures: Em-dash, small pencil icon graphic, em-dash, then the italic bold heading 'We Remember', all on one line.

braille.notes: Line 1 blank; line 2 the cell-5 heading, opening with a transcriber-defined shape indicator for the pencil icon (surrounded by blank spaces per 4.9.1) followed by 'We Remember' (single-capital indicator on each word, i.e. mixed/title case, not full caps).

uncertain: The exact transcriber-defined shape code used for the pencil icon ('@$p' in the source ASCII) was not cross-checked against a Special Symbols page or a UEB shape-indicator reference table; transcribed verbatim as it appears in the source.
resolution: braille.lines agree. `level` resolved to 2 (cell-5, matching run B) rather than run A's null: the braille's 4-cell indent (after the shape-indicator token) is unambiguous.
